strings.name: Marina Abramovic
strings.role: Performance artist · Body, time and audiences
strings.summary: Abramović uses the body, duration and relationships with audiences as artistic materials. The early Rhythm works confronted risk and limits; collaborations with Ulay explored trust, dependence and separation. Balkan Baroque addressed war trauma, while The Artist Is Present staged encounters through prolonged silent sitting. She brought performance into museums and investigated re-performance and preservation; recent exhibitions also emphasize audiences’ sensory participation.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1946–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Explored the body, time and trust through durational performance and audience participation, bringing performance art to international museums and wider public attention.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: The audience relationship as artwork
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: The Artist Is Present turned viewing into a shared, sustained encounter through prolonged silent sitting.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Bodies, trust and history
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: From Rhythm 0 to Balkan Baroque, bodily action becomes a way to examine audience power, risk and historical trauma.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Transforming Energy opens in Venice
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Historical works and interactive stone and crystal installations invited visitors to participate through bodily experience.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: A Royal Academy retrospective opens
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The London exhibition surveyed decades of performance and used re-performance to consider how bodily works can continue in museums.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Presents The Artist Is Present at MoMA
strings.timeline.event-03.text: During the New York retrospective she sat silently opposite visitors for extended periods, placing face-to-face encounter at the work’s center.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Presents Seven Easy Pieces
strings.timeline.event-04.text: At the Guggenheim in New York she re-performed historical works by herself and others, examining performance’s transmission and renewal.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Balkan Baroque wins Venice’s Golden Lion
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Sustained actions including washing bloody bones addressed the Balkan wars through personal origins, collective memory and violence’s residues.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Completes the Great Wall walk with Ulay
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Walking from opposite ends of the Great Wall in China, the pair marked the end of a phase in their artistic and personal partnership.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Performs Rhythm 0 in Naples
strings.timeline.event-07.text: For six hours she let visitors use an array of objects on her body, exposing tensions between participation, responsibility and violence.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Completes studies in Belgrade
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Painting training gave way to increasingly bodily artistic experiments, followed by postgraduate study in Zagreb.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Belgrade
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Born and raised in Yugoslavia, she later reflected on family discipline, religion and postwar society through her work.
